# Camera

Namespace `Nfty.Model.Render` in assembly `Nfty.Model`.

```csharp
public sealed class Camera
```

An immutable turntable-orbit camera: [`Camera.ViewProjection()`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#m-viewprojection-system-int32-system-int32) is the one function that owns the view and projection mapping together, and every other mapping (picking, zoom-anchoring) derives from it or its inverse rather than restating the matrices beside it.

## Remarks

Immutable by the same rule [`Mesh`](Nfty.Model.Mesh.md) states for itself: every value is fixed at construction, so a [`Camera`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md) may be read from many threads and a caller can never hold a half-updated one. Every apparent mutator ([`Camera.Orbit()`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#m-orbit-system-single-system-single), [`Camera.Pan()`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#m-pan-system-numerics-vector2-system-int32), [`Camera.Zoom()`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#m-zoom-system-single), [`Camera.ZoomAnchored()`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#m-zoomanchored-system-single-system-numerics-vector2-sys-d064a7), [`Camera.Reset()`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#m-reset-system-numerics-vector3-system-numerics-vector3-0c7a99)) returns a new instance.

## Constructors

### Camera(Vector3, float, float, float, Vector3, Vector3) { #m-ctor-system-numerics-vector3-system-single-system-sing-4ce45d }

```csharp
public Camera(Vector3 target, float distance, float yaw, float pitch, Vector3 boundsMin, Vector3 boundsMax);
```

Builds a camera, clamping `target` into the box, and `distance` and `pitch` into range, so every instance that exists is already valid. The box sets the distance limits and clip planes.

**Parameters**

- `target` (`Vector3`) - The point orbited and looked at; clamped into the box.
- `distance` (`float`) - Eye-to-target distance; clamped to [`Camera.MinDistance`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#p-mindistance)..[`Camera.MaxDistance`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#p-maxdistance).
- `yaw` (`float`) - Orbit angle around the vertical axis, radians.
- `pitch` (`float`) - Orbit angle above level, radians; clamped.
- `boundsMin` (`Vector3`) - Minimum corner of the subject's box.
- `boundsMax` (`Vector3`) - Maximum corner of the subject's box.

The vertical field of view every projection this camera builds uses.

### PitchLimitDegrees { #f-pitchlimitdegrees }

```csharp
public const float PitchLimitDegrees = 89f;
```

Pitch never exceeds this many degrees from level, either direction — an extruded sprite has a definite up, and a camera rolled onto its side shows an orientation that means nothing.

### LightDirection { #p-lightdirection }

```csharp
public Vector3 LightDirection { get; }
```

The direction TOWARD the light, in world space: a head light riding the camera, up and a little to the left of the eye, so whatever faces the viewer is brightest at any orbit angle. Always a unit vector.

### MaxDistance { #p-maxdistance }

```csharp
public float MaxDistance { get; }
```

Farthest the eye may orbit from its target: `20 ×`.

### MinDistance { #p-mindistance }

```csharp
public float MinDistance { get; }
```

Closest the eye may orbit to its target for the CURRENT orientation: the distance from [`Camera.Target`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#p-target) along the eye direction to where that ray exits the subject's box, plus `0.02 ×`. With the target inside the box this keeps the eye outside it from every angle, yet lets a flat sprite viewed head-on be inspected from just in front of its face. Depends on the orientation, so orbiting at the floor pushes the eye out as the exit distance grows.

Half the box diagonal, in world units (at least 1e-3). The far limit and every clip plane scale with it, so a 16px sprite and a 1000px one behave alike.

### FramedOn(Vector3, Vector3, float) { #m-framedon-system-numerics-vector3-system-numerics-vecto-161a10 }

```csharp
public static Camera FramedOn(Vector3 min, Vector3 max, float aspect = 1f);
```

A camera framing the given bounds: centered on the box, pulled back to fit its bounding sphere in the NARROWER of the vertical and horizontal fields of view (so a tall viewport, `aspect` below 1, does not crop sideways) with 15% margin, looking square-on at the front face (yaw 0, pitch 0) with the box center on the viewport center.

**Parameters**

- `min` (`Vector3`)
- `max` (`Vector3`)
- `aspect` (`float`)

### WithSubject(Vector3, Vector3) { #m-withsubject-system-numerics-vector3-system-numerics-vector3 }

```csharp
public Camera WithSubject(Vector3 min, Vector3 max);
```

The same view (target, distance, orientation) over a new subject box: the radius, the distance limits and the target's confinement follow the box, the camera does not jump (the target is only moved if it would fall outside, the distance only if it would break the floor).

**Parameters**

- `min` (`Vector3`) - Minimum corner of the new box.
- `max` (`Vector3`) - Maximum corner of the new box.

### ZoomAnchored(float, Vector2, int, int) { #m-zoomanchored-system-single-system-numerics-vector2-sys-d064a7 }

```csharp
public Camera ZoomAnchored(float factor, Vector2 pointerScreen, int width, int height);
```

A new camera zoomed by `factor` such that the world point under `pointerScreen` stays under it, to within a pixel. Two passes: zoom around [`Camera.Target`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#p-target) (trivially exact for whatever [`Camera.Target`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#p-target) itself projects to, since [`Camera.ViewProjection()`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#m-viewprojection-system-int32-system-int32) always centers [`Camera.Target`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#p-target) on screen), then a corrective pan that cancels the screen-space error the zoom introduced for the off-center anchor point. That correction does NOT go through the public [`Camera.Pan()`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#m-pan-system-numerics-vector2-system-int32) — [`Camera.Pan()`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#m-pan-system-numerics-vector2-system-int32) converts pixels to world units using [`Camera.Distance`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#p-distance) (the eye-to-Target depth), which is exact only for a point sitting exactly at [`Camera.Target`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#p-target)'s depth; the anchor is generally off that plane. Because a pan perpendicular to the forward axis never changes a fixed point's depth along that axis (the shift has zero component along forward by construction), the anchor's own forward-axis depth is constant through the correction, so converting the screen-space error to world units at THAT depth — instead of at [`Camera.Distance`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md#p-distance) — makes the correction exact in one pass rather than an approximation that needs iterating. Exact while the corrected target stays inside the subject box; over empty space far beside the model the target clamp wins and the anchor drifts — orbiting about empty air is what the clamp exists to prevent.

**Parameters**

- `factor` (`float`)
- `pointerScreen` (`Vector2`)
- `width` (`int`)
- `height` (`int`)
